newsitem.title: GERMANY: TNT wins fight to save post contract.
newsitem.headline: TNT wins fight to save post contract.

text.p: TNT Logistik said it has won the first round of a fight to save a parcels contract with Deutsche Post AG (DPAG) worth several million marks.
A Bonn court has granted an injunction preventing DPAG from terminating the contract effective June 30 this year, a TNT statement said.
Under the deal signed in 1995, TNT set up a special subsidiary, TNT NetLog, with 105 staff, 35 partner firms and 1,000 vehicles, to transport parcels in containers between DPAG freight centres.

But Deutsche Post cancelled the agreement in February on the grounds that TNT was now owned by its competitor, the Dutch post office (Koninklijke PTT Nederland N.V.) and KPN could thus see DPAG internal information.
Vinzenz Wagner, chairman of TNT Holding, said: "We are delighted with this success. We see the decision of the court as a good basis for continued good cooperation with Deutsche Post."

TNT was very confident the court would uphold the validity of the contract, due to run until March 31, 2000, in a full judgement later this year, he added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax: 5017
